title: Ample powers supply a section of an ideal near a point outside its zero set
statement: Let $Y$ be a quasi-compact scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], $\mathcal M$ an ample invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], and $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ a quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent] ideal sheaf. If $y\notin V(\mathcal J)$, there are $n>0$ and $u\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J\mathcal M^{\otimes n})$ with $y\in Y_u$ (viewing $u$ also as a section of $\mathcal M^{\otimes n}$).

source.place: Properties Proposition 01Q3 (properties-proposition-characterize-ample), equivalence of (1) and (6), ideal-sheaf global generation

proof.text: *Setup: a principal affine open around $y$.* By condition (2) of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] there are $d\ge1$ and $s\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal M^{\otimes d})$ with $y\in Y_s$ and $U:=Y_s$ an affine open of $Y$, where $Y_s=\{x\in Y: s_x\notin\mathfrak m_x(\mathcal M^{\otimes d})_x\}$. Put $\mathcal L:=\mathcal M^{\otimes d}$; it is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module], [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $A=\mathcal O_Y(U)$ and, for $x\in U$, let $\mathfrak p_x\subset A$ be the prime of $x$ under $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points].

source.place: Properties Proposition 01Q3 (properties-proposition-characterize-ample), proof, second paragraph: 'Choose $s\in S_+$ homogeneous such that $X_s$ is affine'; Definition 01PS (properties-definition-ample)

proof.text:
*A function in $\mathcal J(U)$ which is a unit at $y$.* $\mathcal J$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and $y\in U$ with $y
otin V(\mathcal J)$, i.e. $\mathcal J_y=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-zero-set-affine] (applied to $\mathcal K=\mathcal J$ and the affine open $U$), $\mathcal J(U)
ot\subseteq\mathfrak p_y$; choose $f\in\mathcal J(U)\subseteq A$ with $f
otin\mathfrak p_y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] (c) the germ $f_y\in\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is a unit.

source.place: Properties Proposition 01Q3, proof, second paragraph (a section $m\in\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal F)$ for $\mathcal F=\mathcal I$ a quasi-coherent ideal, (5) $\Rightarrow$ (6)); the choice of $m$ nonzero at $x$ is implicit in the third paragraph: 'a section $s$ ... such that $s$ does not vanish at $x$'

proof.text: *$Y$ is quasi-compact and separated over an affine scheme.* $Y$ is quasi-compact by hypothesis (also by condition (1) of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]) and separated, i.e. $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated, by [lem-weil-pbc-ample-scheme-separated]; $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is affine.

source.place: Properties Proposition 01Q3, proof, second paragraph: 'Note that in particular $X$ is separated (as an open subscheme of the separated scheme $\operatorname{Proj}(S)$)'; here via Lemma 09MP (properties-lemma-ample-separated)

proof.text: *$Y_s$ is the complement of the zero scheme of $s$.* Let $Z(s)$ be the zero scheme of $s\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal L)$ [def-pc-zero-scheme], cut out by the quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I=\operatorname{im}(s^\vee:\mathcal L^\vee\to\mathcal O_Y)$. On an open $W$ with a trivialization $\mathcal L|_W\cong\mathcal O_W$ [def-sc-invertible-module] sending $s|_W$ to $a\in\mathcal O_Y(W)$, one has $\mathcal I|_W=a\mathcal O_W$, so for $x\in W$: $\mathcal I_x=\mathcal O_{Y,x}$ iff $a_x$ is a unit iff $s_x\notin\mathfrak m_x\mathcal L_x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-zero-set-affine] the underlying set of $Z(s)$ is $V(\mathcal I)=\{x:\mathcal I_x\ne\mathcal O_{Y,x}\}$; hence $Y\setminus Z(s)=Y_s=U$.

source.place: Properties, Section 01PR (properties-section-ample), opening paragraph ($X_s$ is where $s$ does not vanish)

proof.text: *Clearing the denominator.* Apply [lem-pc-section-clearing-denominators] to the quasi-compact scheme $Y$, separated over the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ (Step 3), the invertible module $\mathcal L$, its section $s$ (with $Y\setminus Z(s)=U$ by Step 4), the quasi-coherent module $\mathcal F=\mathcal J$ and $t=f\in\mathcal J(U)=\Gamma(Y_s,\mathcal J)$ (Step 2): there are $m\ge0$ and $u'\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes m})$ with $u'|_U=f\otimes s^m$. Since $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}=(\mathcal M^{\otimes d})^{\otimes m}=\mathcal M^{\otimes dm}$ (associativity of the tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]), $u'$ is a section of $\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal M^{\otimes dm}$.

source.place: Properties Proposition 01Q3, proof, second paragraph: 'by Lemma 01PW (properties-lemma-invert-s-sections) we may write $m$ as the image of $m'\otimes s^{-n}$ for some $n\ge1$, some $m'\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$'

proof.text: *The section $u$ and $n>0$.* Put $n=d(m+1)\ge1$. Let $\mu:\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal M^{\otimes n}\to\mathcal M^{\otimes n}$ be the multiplication map (the inclusion $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ tensored with $\mathcal M^{\otimes n}$, followed by $\mathcal O_Y\otimes\mathcal M^{\otimes n}=\mathcal M^{\otimes n}$); $\mathcal J\mathcal M^{\otimes n}\subseteq\mathcal M^{\otimes n}$ is its image sheaf. Set $u:=\mu(u'\otimes s)\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal M^{\otimes n})$, where $u'\otimes s\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal M^{\otimes dm}\otimes\mathcal M^{\otimes d})=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal M^{\otimes n})$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. As $u$ is the image under $\mu$ of a global section, $u\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J\mathcal M^{\otimes n})$ (the image presheaf is contained in the image sheaf). By Step 5, $u|_U=f\cdot s^{m+1}|_U$, with $s^{m+1}=s\otimes\dots\otimes s\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal M^{\otimes n})$.

source.place: Properties Proposition 01Q3, proof, third paragraph: 'there exists an $n\ge1$ and a section $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$ ... We may think of $s$ as a section of $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$'

proof.text: *$y\in Y_u$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes] applied to $\mathcal L$ and $s$, $\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal L|_U$, $a\mapsto a\,s|_U$, is an isomorphism; tensoring $m+1$ copies, $\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal M^{\otimes n}|_U$, $a\mapsto a\,s^{m+1}|_U$, is an isomorphism [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. On stalks at $y$ it is an isomorphism $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to(\mathcal M^{\otimes n})_y$ of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-modules carrying $\mathfrak m_y$ onto $\mathfrak m_y(\mathcal M^{\otimes n})_y$ and $f_y$ to $u_y$ (Step 6). Since $f_y$ is a unit (Step 2), $f_y\notin\mathfrak m_y$, hence $u_y\notin\mathfrak m_y(\mathcal M^{\otimes n})_y$, i.e. $y\in Y_u$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Thus $n>0$ and $u\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J\mathcal M^{\otimes n})$ are as claimed.

source.place: Properties Proposition 01Q3, proof, third paragraph: 'such that $s$ does not vanish at $x$ (more precisely such that $s\notin\mathfrak m_x\mathcal I_x\otimes\mathcal L_x^{\otimes n}$)'

split_report.summary: Split following Stacks 01Q3 (properties-proposition-characterize-ample), the part (1) => (5) => (6) of its proof specialized to F = J and the point y: choose s in Gamma(Y, M^d) with y in Y_s affine (definition 01PS); pick f in J(Y_s) not in p_y (zero set of a quasi-coherent ideal on an affine); Y is separated (09MP); Lemma 01PW (the Lean-closed lem-pc-section-clearing-denominators, with Y_s identified with the complement of Z(s)) gives u' in Gamma(Y, J (x) M^{dm}) restricting to f s^m; u = mu(u' (x) s) lies in Gamma(Y, J M^{d(m+1)}) and its germ at y is f_y times a basis. Statement kept (the hypothesis 'quasi-compact' is redundant, ampleness includes it). No new nodes; no slopmaster2 declaration states the item. The source deduces separatedness from the open immersion into Proj (01Q1); the split uses 09MP instead, which is the same fact by a shorter route. A factor s is multiplied in to make n = d(m+1) > 0 since 01PW may return m = 0.
